headline: Quarterly loss narrows, but tariffs squeeze annual margins
summary_short: Under Armour's fiscal Q4 net revenue was $1,171.2M, roughly flat y/y (-0.8%) though down 11.8% q/q on seasonality; the net loss narrowed to $(43.4)M ($(0.10) diluted EPS) from $(67.5)M a year earlier, even as full-year FY2026 gross margin fell 240bps to 45.5% on tariffs.
summary_long: Quarterly (fiscal Q4) net revenue of $1,171.2M was roughly flat y/y but down 11.8% q/q on normal seasonality. The net loss narrowed to $(43.4)M ($(0.10) diluted EPS) from $(67.5)M y/y and improved sharply from a $(430.8)M prior-quarter loss tied to one-off charges. For full fiscal-year 2026, revenue fell 3.8% and gross margin compressed 240bps to 45.5%, driven mainly by tariffs (155bps) and unfavorable pricing/mix; the 2025 restructuring plan was expanded in May 2026 to ~$305M. Cash fell to $309.2M after depositing $601.2M into restricted investments to defease the 2026 Senior Notes; long-term debt rose to $1,190.4M on a new $400M note issuance, while $599.8M of the discharged 2026 notes now sit in short-term debt pending June 2026 maturity.

drivers.explanation: This is UA's FY2026 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2026). Shard KPIs above are for the March-2026 quarter only, but the 10-K's MD&A covers the full year: revenue -3.8%, gross margin -240bps to 45.5% on tariffs, restructuring plan expanded to ~$305M in May 2026.

10-K discusses only full-year results (no Q4-specific breakout). FY2026 net revenue fell 3.8% on North America (-7.9%) and Asia-Pacific (-4.8%) softness, partly offset by EMEA (+8.6%) and Latin America (+8.7%) growth.

Full-year only: FY2026 gross margin fell 240bps to 45.5%, driven by 155bps of tariff impact, 70bps unfavorable pricing and 45bps channel/regional mix, partly offset by 45bps favorable FX and 20bps product mix.

Full-year only: North America operating income fell $187.0M (-29.7%) on lower gross profit and higher tariff-driven input costs, partly offset by lower facility costs from exiting the Rialto, CA distribution center; EMEA operating income rose $44.3M.

Full-year interest expense rose $24.2M to $30.3M on the new 2030 Senior Notes and revolver draws; litigation reserve expense was $98.5M in FY2026 vs $261M in FY2025; a full valuation allowance was recorded against all US federal deferred tax assets.
Mirrors the swing in operating income once depreciation and amortization is added back; the filing does not report a standalone quarterly EBITDA bridge.

Cash fell as $601.2M was deposited into restricted investments in August 2025 to satisfy and discharge the Senior Notes due 2026, plus $87.1M of capex, partly offset by $400M of new Senior Notes and net revolver borrowings.
Reflects the June 2025 issuance of $400M Senior Notes due 2030 plus $200M outstanding on the revolving credit facility as of March 31, 2026 (borrowed $490M, repaid $290M during the year).

The $600M Senior Notes due 2026 were reclassified to current as they approach June 2026 maturity; they were economically satisfied and discharged in August 2025 via a restricted-investment deposit but remain on the balance sheet until maturity.

Decline is consistent with the year's net losses and $25M of Class C share repurchases (of a $500M program, $115M repurchased to date); the filing does not provide a full equity roll-forward breakdown.
